sections.label: Frozen accounts and traced funds
sections.summary: SPF froze 121 local bank accounts, recovered about $2 million, traced $2.2 million to 89 overseas accounts, and linked 107 local and 171 overseas IP addresses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: As at 13 February, SPF has frozen 121 local bank accounts and recovered about $2 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In addition, about $2.2 million of victims’ funds have been traced to 89 overseas bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Based on SPF’s preliminary investigations, at least 107 local and 171 overseas IP addresses were linked to the unauthorised access of the victims’ Internet banking accounts.

sections.label: Scam and phishing case numbers
sections.summary: In 2021, 23,931 scam cases were reported, of which 5,020 were phishing scam cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2021, 23,931 cases of scams were reported, of which 5,020 were phishing scam cases.

sections.label: Anti-scam coordination efforts
sections.summary: ASC and MAS are working with more banks to co-locate staff, and SPF will form an Anti-Scam Command this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: ASC and MAS are working with more banks to co-locate their staff at the ASC, to further enhance the ASC’s capabilities to freeze accounts, as well as to trace the flows of money.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: SPF will be forming an Anti-Scam Command this year to consolidate expertise in scams across all SPF land units, and thereby further improve coordination of anti-scam enforcement and investigation.

sections.label: Victim age groups by scam type
sections.summary: Young adults aged 20 to 39 formed the largest victim group for several scams, while adults aged 40 to 59 formed the largest group for others.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For phishing scams, job scams, e-commerce scams, investment scams, loan scams, China official impersonation scams, as well as fake gambling platform scams, we found that young adults between 20 and 39 years old formed the largest group of victims, compared to other age groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For social media impersonation scams, Internet love scams, and fake friend call scams, adults between 40 and 59 years old formed the largest group of victims.

sections.label: ScamShield downloads and blocks
sections.summary: ScamShield has been downloaded about 257,000 times, picked up about 3.5 million SMSes and calls, and blocked about 15,500 phone numbers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To date, ScamShield has been downloaded about 257,000 times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: About 3.5 million SMSes and calls have been picked up as potential scams by the in-app algorithm and user self-reporting through the app.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: About 15,500 phone numbers have also been blocked.

sections.label: Android version in development
sections.summary: Agencies are working towards developing and releasing the Android version in the coming few months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Agencies are now working towards developing and releasing the Android version in the coming few months.

sections.label: Loss-sharing framework for scam losses
sections.summary: MAS-chaired Payments Council is deliberating a common, equitable framework for sharing scam losses, with public consultation within three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the framework for the sharing of losses incurred by customers, this is a complex issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I mentioned just now that it is being deliberated upon by the Payments Council, which is chaired by MAS, and it aims to put up something for public consultation within the next three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, the framework for the sharing of losses should be consistent and common.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Second, the framework should be equitable in determining how losses are to be shared, because both banks and customers have their respective responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But what we intend to do is to be quite clear and specific about what these responsibilities are for financial institutions and customers and what each party is expected to do to prevent scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Then, the share of losses each party bears will depend on whether and how the party has fallen short of these very clearly stated responsibilities.

sections.label: Measures across retail banks
sections.summary: MAS and ABS put in place a comprehensive suite of measures and controls across all retail banks, and MAS is studying further enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Amongst the three local banks, this started last year, following MAS' focus supervisory review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Then, earlier this year, in January, as I mentioned just now, MAS and ABS put in place a comprehensive suite of measures and controls that will apply across all retail banks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is, in fact, more than what major jurisdictions have in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And we are going beyond that, because, as I have highlighted in my speech, MAS is also considering and studying further enhancements to the measures that we can put in place across banks to reduce the risk across our digital banking channels.

sections.label: Financial institutions bearing losses
sections.summary: Financial institutions that fall short of their responsibilities should bear their share of the losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Indeed, if financial institutions were to fall short of these responsibilities, then they should bear their share of the losses.

sections.label: SMS issuance and OTP deception
sections.summary: Even through a safe encrypted channel, SMS issuance would not stop deception, and a person with the OTP will still provide it to a scam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Issuance of SMS, even if it were to be done through a very safe and encrypted channel, for example, that would not stop deception from happening and, if the scam succeeds in identity theft, as has happened here, impersonating a bank, getting the person to think that this is, in fact, a genuine bank, then the person with the OTP will still provide the OTP to this scam website or scam account or whatever it is.

sections.label: SDOs reaching seniors
sections.summary: The SDOs have reached out to 130,000 seniors at community centres, libraries and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Today, the SDOs have done a good job in reaching out to 130,000 seniors in our community at the community centres, different libraries and so on.

sections.label: MAS studying global loss-sharing models
sections.summary: MAS will look at models around the world for the loss-sharing framework, and responsibility differs for individuals and financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Number one: MAS will certainly look at models around the world in developing the details of this framework for the sharing of losses in an equitable fair share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Number two: as the Member has highlighted, the responsibility will be different for individuals and financial institutions.

sections.label: Foreign agency scam cooperation
sections.summary: MHA and SPF will build networks with foreign law enforcement agencies and work with Interpol to investigate across jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I just wanted to check whether there is any framework in place for us to actually cooperate with foreign agencies in order to identify the perpetrators and have them prosecuted for these actions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: I mentioned in my speech that this is an area that MHA and SPF will continue to sharpen, to build our networks across the different foreign law enforcement agencies as well as working with Interpol to enhance our ability to respond and to investigate across jurisdictions.

sections.label: MAS customer confirmation for transactions
sections.summary: MAS is introducing additional customer confirmations for higher-risk transactions including large and overseas fund transfers, and cooling-off periods have been done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my speech, MAS is, indeed, looking to introduce additional customer confirmations for higher-risk transactions, and that would include fund transfers that are large, relative to the overall balances, as well as overseas transfers, recognising that once the funds leave our local banking system, they are very hard to recover, indeed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, as I have mentioned, these are additional strengthening and enhancements we are looking at, which will require customer confirmation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It will add friction to the transaction for genuine customers but we hope that everyone understands that these inconveniences are necessary to have a safer digital banking system in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The second point about having a cooling-off period, if the banks are aware of the scam and whether or not they can put in place some cooling-off periods, indeed, that is something that has been done.

sections.label: MAS standards for scam victim management
sections.summary: MAS sets standards for banks in managing scam victims, and OCBC's conduct is being reviewed with appropriate actions to follow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask if the Ministry, or the agencies in charge of this, will be putting in standards and requirements for the banks in the management of scam victims during the investigation process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But I should clarify the standards are not set by MOF; they are set by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and I am speaking also in my capacity as the Deputy Chairman of MAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There were areas, in terms of its responses to customers, which, certainly, could be improved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why we are reviewing the conduct of OCBC, and we will take the appropriate actions.

sections.label: DNS blocking and VoIP calls
sections.summary: Current call and website blocking is mainly done through DNS blocking, which does not block VoIP calls.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The current call blocking, as well as the website blocking, is now mainly done through Domain Name System (DNS) blocking.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, unless my technical understanding is flawed, and I would have to check this up, my understanding is that it does not block VoIP calls.
